title: Set Operations (UNION, UNION ALL, INTERSECT, EXCEPT) Narration Scripts

lecture.New_Day12Part1audio01.mp3: Welcome to Day 12! Today, we explore SQL Set Operations: UNION, UNION ALL, INTERSECT, and EXCEPT. While Joins stitch tables together horizontally by matching columns, Set Operations stack query results vertically, treating outputs as mathematical sets.
lecture.New_Day12Part1audio02.mp3: Set operations require strict schema compatibility between queries: both SELECT statements must return the exact same number of columns, and corresponding columns must have compatible data types.
lecture.New_Day12Part1audio03.mp3: Column names in the final result set are always inherited from the first SELECT statement, regardless of what aliases are used in subsequent queries.
lecture.New_Day12Part1audio04.mp3: The foundational set operator is UNION. UNION combines rows from both queries and automatically deduplicates the output, returning only distinct records.
lecture.New_Day12Part1audio05.mp3: In Query 1, we combine email addresses from employees and customers into a single, deduplicated master contact list.
lecture.New_Day12Part1audio06.mp3: Next is UNION ALL. Unlike UNION, UNION ALL retains every single row from both queries, including duplicates, without performing an expensive sort-and-deduplication pass.
lecture.New_Day12Part1audio07.mp3: Performance best practice: Whenever you know rows between two queries cannot overlap, or when duplicates are acceptable, always default to UNION ALL for lightning-fast execution.
lecture.New_Day12Part1audio08.mp3: In Query 2, we consolidate all employee and customer names with a source label, using UNION ALL to preserve every record.
lecture.New_Day12Part1audio09.mp3: Now, let's explore INTERSECT. INTERSECT returns only rows that are present in both the first and second query results, effectively calculating the common overlap between two sets.
lecture.New_Day12Part1audio10.mp3: In Query 3, we use INTERSECT to find first names that appear in both the customer roster and the employee staff list.
lecture.New_Day12Part1audio11.mp3: The final operation is EXCEPT, also known as MINUS in Oracle. EXCEPT returns rows from the first query that do not exist in the second query.
lecture.New_Day12Part1audio12.mp3: In Query 4, we use EXCEPT to instantly identify registered customers who have never placed an order.
lecture.New_Day12Part1audio13.mp3: Sorting set operations: The ORDER BY clause can only appear once, at the very end of the entire compound statement, and applies globally to the combined result set.
lecture.New_Day12Part1audio14.mp3: In Query 5, we combine financial revenue and payroll expenses into a unified ledger, sorted by metric name.
lecture.New_Day12Part1audio15.mp3: Cross-database comparison: UNION and UNION ALL are universal across all SQL engines. INTERSECT and EXCEPT are natively supported in SQLite, PostgreSQL, SQL Server, and Snowflake, but require subqueries or joins in older MySQL versions.
lecture.New_Day12Part1audio16.mp3: You're now ready to combine datasets vertically with mathematical precision! Let's enter the practice arena and solve multi-source data consolidation challenges.

questions.New_Day12Question01.mp3: Master email directory! Combine email addresses from employees and customers into a single sorted list with no duplicates using UNION.
questions.New_Day12Question01sol.mp3: Let's combine emails with UNION. SELECT email FROM employees UNION SELECT email FROM customers ORDER BY email.
questions.New_Day12Question02.mp3: Consolidate contacts with source tags! Return first name, last name, and an entity type label of Employee from employees, combined with first name, last name, and Customer from customers using UNION ALL.
questions.New_Day12Question02sol.mp3: Let's stack contacts with UNION ALL. SELECT first_name, last_name, 'Employee' AS entity_type FROM employees UNION ALL SELECT first_name, last_name, 'Customer' AS entity_type FROM customers ORDER BY last_name, first_name.
questions.New_Day12Question03.mp3: Unique first names directory! Return all distinct first names across both employees and customers using UNION, ordered alphabetically.
questions.New_Day12Question03sol.mp3: Let's get unique first names. SELECT first_name FROM employees UNION SELECT first_name FROM customers ORDER BY first_name.
questions.New_Day12Question04.mp3: Deduplicate order statuses! Query order status from orders combined with order status from orders using UNION to return unique status values.
questions.New_Day12Question04sol.mp3: Let's deduplicate statuses. SELECT status FROM orders UNION SELECT status FROM orders.
questions.New_Day12Question05.mp3: Shared names discovery! Find first names that exist in both the customers table and the employees table using INTERSECT.
questions.New_Day12Question05sol.mp3: Let's find overlapping names with INTERSECT. SELECT first_name FROM customers INTERSECT SELECT first_name FROM employees.
questions.New_Day12Question06.mp3: Active customer ID audit! Return customer IDs that exist in both customers and orders using INTERSECT.
questions.New_Day12Question06sol.mp3: Let's intersect active customer IDs. SELECT customer_id FROM customers INTERSECT SELECT customer_id FROM orders WHERE customer_id IS NOT NULL.
questions.New_Day12Question07.mp3: Identify inactive customer IDs with EXCEPT! Find customer IDs from customers that do not appear in the orders table using EXCEPT.
questions.New_Day12Question07sol.mp3: Let's find inactive IDs with EXCEPT. SELECT customer_id FROM customers EXCEPT SELECT customer_id FROM orders WHERE customer_id IS NOT NULL.
questions.New_Day12Question08.mp3: Unsold products detection! Find product IDs from products that have never been recorded in order items using EXCEPT.
questions.New_Day12Question08sol.mp3: Let's isolate unsold products. SELECT product_id FROM products EXCEPT SELECT product_id FROM order_items.
questions.New_Day12Question09.mp3: Active categories with inventory! Find category IDs that exist in both the categories table and the products table using INTERSECT.
questions.New_Day12Question09sol.mp3: Let's find active categories with INTERSECT. SELECT id AS category_id FROM categories INTERSECT SELECT category_id FROM products WHERE category_id IS NOT NULL.
questions.New_Day12Question10.mp3: VIP entities unified ledger! Combine high-value order customer IDs with executive staff employee IDs into a single list of entity IDs with tags using UNION.
questions.New_Day12Question10sol.mp3: Let's combine VIP entities. SELECT customer_id AS entity_id, 'High-Value Customer' AS tag FROM orders WHERE total_amount >= 50000 UNION SELECT employee_id AS entity_id, 'Executive Staff' AS tag FROM employees WHERE salary >= 100000.
questions.New_Day12Question11.mp3: Empty categories audit! Return category ID and name from categories that have no products assigned to them using EXCEPT.
questions.New_Day12Question11sol.mp3: Let's find empty categories with EXCEPT. SELECT id AS category_id, name AS category_name FROM categories EXCEPT SELECT c.id, c.name FROM categories c INNER JOIN products p ON c.id = p.category_id.
questions.New_Day12Question12.mp3: Target outreach directory! Combine Data Science employees with North region customers using UNION ALL, returning first name, last name, and role.
questions.New_Day12Question12sol.mp3: Let's combine outreach targets. SELECT first_name, last_name, 'Employee' AS role FROM employees WHERE department_id = 20 UNION ALL SELECT first_name, last_name, 'VIP Customer' AS role FROM customers WHERE region = 'North' ORDER BY role, first_name.
questions.New_Day12Question13.mp3: Consolidated status roster! Combine active employees, inactive employees, and customers into one list of first name and email using UNION, sorted by email.
questions.New_Day12Question13sol.mp3: Let's combine three rosters. SELECT first_name, email FROM employees WHERE is_active = 1 UNION SELECT first_name, email FROM employees WHERE is_active = 0 UNION SELECT first_name, email FROM customers ORDER BY email.
questions.New_Day12Question14.mp3: Company financial flow ledger! Combine total order revenue with total employee payroll in a single summary table using UNION ALL.
questions.New_Day12Question14sol.mp3: Let's combine financial summaries. SELECT 'Total Revenue' AS metric, SUM of total_amount AS amount FROM orders UNION ALL SELECT 'Total Payroll' AS metric, SUM of salary AS amount FROM employees.
questions.New_Day12Question15.mp3: Customer lifecycle segmentation with UNION! Label customers with orders as Active Buyer and customers without orders as Prospect, returning first name, last name, and customer status.
questions.New_Day12Question15sol.mp3: Let's segment customer lifecycles. SELECT c.first_name, c.last_name, 'Active Buyer' AS customer_status FROM customers c INNER JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id UNION SELECT c.first_name, c.last_name, 'Prospect' AS customer_status FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.order_id IS NULL ORDER BY customer_status, first_name.
